description: Try a grades 6-8 ACCESS-style model practice test with test-like directions, item numbers, review, and teacher scripts.

6-8-A.range: Classroom support choice; not a WIDA proficiency level
6-8-A.studentGoal: I can practice a test-like routine and show what I understand.
6-8-A.objective: I can answer listening and reading items and write or say short evidence responses.
6-8-A.target: Today I will practice the process of a language test: listen, read, choose, explain, and review.

activities.title: Before You Begin
activities.testFormat: Grades 6-8 · Level A · Unofficial classroom model
activities.directions: Read the practice-test directions. Choose the answer that shows what students should do during the test.
vocabulary: practice that looks like a test
examen de práctica: práctica que parece un examen
instrucciones: lo que hay que hacer
frames: During this practice test, I will ___.
If I am unsure, I will ___.
activities.prompt: Directions: Read or listen to each item. Choose the best answer. For speaking or writing items, use the frame and give evidence.

options.text: Choose the best answer and explain with evidence when asked.
Click answers as fast as possible without reading.
Skip every question with academic words.

activities.correct: Correct. This practice test asks you to slow down, choose the best answer, and use evidence.
activities.hint: Look for the answer that matches careful test behavior.
activities.support: Model: I read the item, choose the best answer, and explain when asked.
activities.extension: Say: During this practice test, I will ___.
activities.adminScript: Say: This is a classroom model practice test. It is not the official ACCESS test. We are practicing the process and language skills.

teacher.use: Use before a station, small-group mock test, or ACCESS prep lesson.
teacher.function: Follow assessment directions and understand expectations.
teacher.lower: Read directions aloud and check student understanding with thumbs up/down.
teacher.onLevel: Students paraphrase the directions with the frame.
teacher.challenge: Students name one strategy for difficult items.
teacher.noTech: Print the directions and have students underline action words.
teacher.prompt: What should students do when they are unsure?

activities.title: Listening Item 1
activities.testFormat: Listen to the teacher statement. Then answer the question.
activities.directions: Listen or read the announcement. Choose the best answer.
vocabulary: anuncio: un mensaje para toda la escuela
activities.prompt: What should students bring?
activities.correct: Correct. The announcement names three materials: notebook, pencil, and safety glasses.
activities.hint: Listen for the list of materials after the word bring.
activities.support: Model: The word bring tells what students need to take to the front table.
activities.extension: Use the frame: The teacher says to bring ___.

teacher.use: Mock Listening item for classroom materials and sequence language.
teacher.function: Identify details in an oral classroom announcement.
teacher.lower: Preview materials with pictures before the item.
teacher.onLevel: Students answer and cite one word of evidence.
teacher.challenge: Students explain why option B is a different school setting.
teacher.noTech: Read the item aloud and have students mark A/B/C.
teacher.prompt: Which words tell the materials?

activities.teacherNote: Read the teacher statement twice at a steady pace. Do not explain the answer before students choose.
activities.script: Before science lab, bring your notebook, pencil, and safety glasses to the front table.

activities.title: Listening Item 2
activities.skill: Identify main idea in academic talk
activities.testFormat: Listen to a short academic statement. Choose the main idea.
activities.directions: Choose what the teacher statement is mostly about.
vocabulary: what the whole message is mostly about
idea principal: de qué trata todo el mensaje
energía: la fuerza para hacer trabajo
activities.prompt: What is this mostly about?

options.text: Different living things and machines need energy.
Food can be hot or cold.

activities.correct: Correct. The whole statement is about energy and who or what needs it.
activities.hint: The best answer should include the big topic, not one small detail.
activities.support: Model: Sun and food are details. The main idea is about energy needs.
activities.extension: Explain: I chose ___ because the statement is mostly about ___.

teacher.function: Summarize short oral academic language.
teacher.lower: Ask students to repeat the topic word energy.
teacher.onLevel: Students identify one detail and the main idea.
teacher.challenge: Students write another detail that fits the same main idea.
teacher.noTech: Students circle the option that is bigger than the details.
teacher.prompt: Which answer covers all the details?

activities.teacherNote: Read the statement twice. Pause before asking the question.
activities.script: Some energy comes from the sun. Some energy comes from food. People, plants, and machines need energy to work or grow.

activities.title: Reading Item 1
activities.testFormat: Read the passage. Then answer the question.
activities.directions: Read the passage and choose the best answer.
vocabulary: comunidad: personas en un mismo lugar
frames: A detail that supports this is ___.
activities.prompt: Passage: A school garden can help a community. Students grow vegetables and learn about plants. Families may use the vegetables for healthy meals. The garden also gives insects and birds a safe place. What is the passage mostly about?

options.text: A school garden can help people and nature.
Birds can fly over a school.

activities.correct: Correct. The passage tells several ways a school garden helps people and nature.
activities.hint: Find the answer that includes more than one detail from the passage.
activities.support: Model: Vegetables, families, insects, and birds are details that support the big idea.
activities.extension: Write: The passage is mostly about ___.
activities.adminScript: Let students read silently first. Then read the question aloud if needed.

teacher.use: Mock Reading item for short informational text.
teacher.function: Determine central idea and supporting details.
teacher.lower: Preteach garden, community, and protect.
teacher.onLevel: Students highlight one detail before answering.
teacher.challenge: Students explain why option C is a detail.
teacher.noTech: Print the passage and answer choices.
teacher.prompt: Which option is the big idea?

activities.title: Reading Item 2
activities.testFormat: Read the chart-style information. Choose the detail.
activities.directions: Use the chart to answer the detail question.
vocabulary: information organized in rows or columns
gráfica o tabla: información en filas o columnas
categoría: un grupo de cosas que van juntas
el menor: la cantidad más pequeña
activities.prompt: Which club has the fewest students?
activities.correct: Correct. Garden Club has 9 students, and 9 is the least amount.
activities.hint: Least means the smallest number. Compare 12, 18, and 9.
activities.support: Model: I compare the numbers. 9 is smaller than 12 and 18.
activities.extension: Say: The least amount is ___.
activities.adminScript: Read the chart information exactly as written. Students may reread the chart.

teacher.function: Interpret chart details and comparative language.
teacher.lower: Review least/smallest before testing.
teacher.onLevel: Students identify the category and number.
teacher.challenge: Students make one more question about the chart.
teacher.noTech: Draw the chart on paper or board.
teacher.prompt: Which number is smallest?

activities.title: Listening Item 3
activities.directions: Read or listen carefully. Choose the best answer.
vocabulary: luego o después: el paso siguiente
write the name of a part
etiquetar: escribir el nombre de una parte
activities.prompt: What should students do first?
activities.correct: Correct. First tells the first action: label the diagram.
activities.hint: Listen for the sequence word first.
activities.support: Use the sentence frame and point to the words that prove your answer.
activities.extension: Explain your choice using because.
activities.teacherNote: Read the item clearly. Students may reread the answer choices.
activities.script: First label the diagram. Next write one sentence about the parts.

activities.title: Reading Item 3
activities.directions: Read or listen carefully. Choose the best answer.
vocabulary: apoyar: ayudar a mostrar que una idea es verdad
biblioteca: lugar para leer y aprender
activities.prompt: Passage: Many students use the library after school. Some read books, some use computers, and some work with tutors. Which detail supports the main idea?

options.text: Students use computers in the library.

activities.correct: Correct. Using computers is one way students use the library after school.
activities.hint: Choose a detail from the passage.
activities.support: Use the sentence frame and point to the words that prove your answer.
activities.extension: Explain your choice using because.
activities.adminScript: Read the item clearly. Students may reread the answer choices.

activities.title: Academic Word Item
activities.directions: Read or listen carefully. Choose the best answer.
activities.prompt: What does describe mean?
activities.correct: Correct. Describe means tell about something using details.
activities.hint: Think about what a student does when asked to describe.
activities.support: Use the sentence frame and point to the words that prove your answer.
activities.extension: Explain your choice using because.
activities.teacherNote: Read the item clearly. Students may reread the answer choices.
activities.script: Describe how the two maps are different.

activities.title: Math Language Item
activities.directions: Read or listen carefully. Choose the best answer.
vocabulary: comparar: decir en qué se parecen o difieren dos cosas
activities.prompt: A class collected 24 cans on Monday and 31 cans on Tuesday. Which sentence is true?

options.text: Tuesday had more cans than Monday.
Monday had more cans than Tuesday.
Both days had the same number.

activities.correct: Correct. 31 is greater than 24, so Tuesday had more.
activities.hint: Compare 24 and 31.
activities.support: Use the sentence frame and point to the words that prove your answer.
activities.extension: Explain your choice using because.
activities.adminScript: Read the item clearly. Students may reread the answer choices.

activities.title: Science Detail Item
activities.directions: Read or listen carefully. Choose the best answer.
vocabulary: causa: la razón por la que algo pasó
activities.prompt: Text: When plants do not get enough water, their leaves may wilt. What can cause leaves to wilt?
activities.correct: Correct. The text says leaves may wilt when plants do not get enough water.
activities.hint: Look after the word when.
activities.support: Use the sentence frame and point to the words that prove your answer.
activities.extension: Explain your choice using because.
activities.adminScript: Read the item clearly. Students may reread the answer choices.

activities.title: Short Response Item
activities.directions: Write or say a short answer with one reason.
vocabulary: afirmación: una idea que dices que es verdad
words or details that prove it
evidencia: palabras que prueban tu respuesta
porque: una palabra que da una razón
activities.prompt: Choose one item from Part A and explain how you knew the answer.
activities.correct: Response saved. A strong answer gives a claim and evidence.
activities.hint: Use the frame and include one clear detail.
activities.support: Model: I think ___ because the text says ___.
activities.extension: Read your response aloud and check for because.
activities.adminScript: Give quiet planning time. Students may respond in writing or orally.
successCriteria: Address the task: Choose one item from Part A and explain how you knew the answer.
Name the process, change, or idea being explained.
Connect a relevant detail to a reason using clear language.

activities.title: Speaking/Writing Response
activities.testFormat: Plan a short response. Say it or write it.
activities.directions: Use the frame to answer. Give one reason.
vocabulary: afirmación: una idea que dices que es verdad
words or numbers that prove it
evidencia: palabras que prueban tu respuesta
activities.prompt: Question: Which school activity from this model test would help students learn the most: science lab, school garden, or robotics? Use one reason.
activities.responsePlaceholder: I think ___ would help students learn the most because ___.
activities.correct: Response saved. A strong response names one activity and gives a reason with because.
activities.hint: Use the frame and include one clear reason.
activities.support: Model: I think science lab would help students learn the most because students use materials and safety glasses.
activities.extension: Read your response aloud to a partner or teacher.
activities.adminScript: Give students quiet planning time. They may say the response to a partner, teacher, or recording tool.

teacher.use: Constructed-response practice after the model selected-response items.
teacher.function: Produce a claim with evidence.
teacher.lower: Provide oral rehearsal with the sentence frame.
teacher.onLevel: Students write or say one complete because sentence.
teacher.challenge: Students add a second evidence sentence.
teacher.noTech: Students answer on paper or orally in a small group.
teacher.prompt: Does the response include a claim and a reason?

successCriteria: Address the task: Question: Which school activity from this model test would help students learn the most: science lab, school garden, or robotics? Use one reason.
Name a relevant person, place, object, or idea.
Add an accurate action or detail that helps someone understand it.

activities.title: Find the Evidence
activities.skill: Locate text evidence for an answer
activities.directions: Read the passage. Click the ONE sentence that best proves the answer to the question.
readFor: the key word in the question
a sentence that states a fact
where the proof is in the text
vocabulary: probar: mostrar que algo es verdad
frames: The evidence is in the sentence ___.
activities.prompt: Click the sentence that proves WHY the city built more bike lanes.
passage: Last year the city counted more bicycles on the road than ever before.
City leaders worried that bikes and cars were too close together.
To keep riders safe, the city painted special bike lanes on busy streets.
Now many families say they feel comfortable riding to school and work.

sentences.text: Last year the city counted more bicycles on the road than ever before.
City leaders worried that bikes and cars were too close together.
To keep riders safe, the city painted special bike lanes on busy streets.
Now many families say they feel comfortable riding to school and work.

activities.correct: Correct. Sentence 3 states the reason: the city built bike lanes to keep riders safe.
activities.hint: A test asks "why," so look for a sentence with a reason word like "to keep."
activities.support: Underline the key word in the question, then scan for the matching sentence.
activities.extension: Find one more sentence that shows the result of the bike lanes.

teacher.function: Locating the proof sentence for a why-question.
teacher.lower: Read the question and circle the key word together.
teacher.challenge: Ask students to label cause and result sentences.
teacher.noTech: Print the passage; students underline the proof.
teacher.prompt: Which word in the question told you what to look for?

activities.title: Pick the Main Idea
activities.skill: Identify the main idea of a passage
activities.directions: Read the short passage. Choose the sentence that tells the MAIN idea, not just one small detail.
readFor: what the whole passage is about
an idea that covers every sentence
vocabulary: idea principal: el punto más importante
tema: de qué trata el texto
activities.prompt: Passage: Sea otters wrap themselves in seaweed so they do not float away while they sleep. They also hold hands with other otters. These habits help otters stay safe in the ocean. What is the main idea?
passage: Sea otters wrap themselves in seaweed so they do not float away while they sleep.
They also hold hands with other otters.
These habits help otters stay safe in the ocean.

options.text: Sea otters use clever habits to stay safe.

activities.correct: Correct. The main idea covers the whole passage: otters use habits to stay safe.
activities.hint: The main idea is bigger than one habit. It covers ALL the sentences.
activities.support: Choices b and c are only single details. The main idea ties them together.
activities.extension: Write your own title that matches the main idea.

teacher.function: Choosing a central idea over a detail.
teacher.lower: Read each option and ask: does it cover everything?
teacher.challenge: Students explain why the detail choices are too narrow.
teacher.noTech: Read aloud; students point to the broadest choice.
teacher.prompt: How is a main idea different from a detail?

activities.title: Listen for Key Words
activities.skill: Use key words to find the answer
activities.directions: Listen to the short talk. Use the key word in the question to find the right answer.
vocabulary: palabra clave: la palabra más importante
a spoken message to a group
anuncio: un mensaje hablado a un grupo
the last day to do something
fecha límite: el último día para algo
frames: I heard ___, so the answer is ___.
activities.prompt: When is the science project due?
activities.correct: Correct. The key word is "due," and the speaker says the project is due on Friday.
activities.hint: The question key word is "due." Listen for the day that comes right after it.
activities.support: When a question asks "when," listen for a day, date, or time.
activities.extension: What should students bring to class on Friday?
activities.adminScript: Good morning, scientists. Your weather poster project is coming along well. Remember, the project is due on Friday, so finish your drawings tonight. We will present them on Monday. Now answer: When is the science project due?

teacher.function: Matching a question key word to the spoken answer.
teacher.lower: Say the key word aloud before reading the question.
teacher.challenge: Add a second date as a distractor.
teacher.noTech: Read aloud; students raise the matching day card.
teacher.prompt: Which word in the question told you to listen for a day?

activities.script: Good morning. Your math homework is due on Monday, and your science project is due on Friday. Picture day is on Sunday.

activities.title: Academic Word Sort
activities.skill: Sort academic test words by meaning
activities.directions: Each phrase tells you what a test word means. Choose the academic word that matches each meaning.
vocabulary: analizar: mirar las partes con cuidado
comparar: decir en qué se parecen
resumir: decir los puntos principales en breve

items.text: Break it into parts and study each one.
Tell how two things are alike or different.
Give the main points in a few sentences.
Use clues to say what will happen next.

activities.correct: Strong work. You matched each academic verb to its meaning.
activities.hint: Listen for the action: studying parts, telling likeness, shortening, or guessing the future.
activities.support: These verbs show up in test directions. Knowing them helps you do the right task.
activities.extension: Write one test question that uses the word "analyze."

teacher.function: Classifying test verbs by meaning.
teacher.lower: Sort only two words first: compare and predict.
teacher.challenge: Students add a fifth verb such as "describe."
teacher.noTech: Cut meanings into strips and match on desks.
teacher.prompt: Which verb tells you to look at the future?

activities.prompt: Sort each one into the best group.

activities.title: Order the Paragraph
activities.directions: Put the sentences in the best order to make a clear paragraph. Use the transition words as clues.
vocabulary: transición: una palabra que une ideas
the first sentence that names the idea
oración temática: la primera oración que nombra la idea
frames: The word ___ shows this sentence comes ___.

items.text: Learning to cook is a useful skill for students.
First, you learn to follow directions carefully.
Next, you practice measuring and mixing.
Finally, cooking helps you eat healthy food you enjoy.

activities.correct: Correct. The topic sentence comes first, then the steps with first/next, then the conclusion.
activities.hint: The topic sentence names the big idea. Then follow first, next, finally.
activities.support: A clear paragraph opens with the idea, builds with transitions, and closes with a result.
activities.extension: Add one more sentence with the transition "in addition."

teacher.function: Sequencing sentences into a coherent paragraph.
teacher.lower: Give students the topic sentence first.
teacher.challenge: Remove transition words and ask students to add them.
teacher.noTech: Cut sentences into strips to arrange on desks.
teacher.prompt: Which word told you the closing sentence?

activities.prompt: Put the steps in the correct order.

activities.title: Choose the Transition
activities.directions: Complete the paragraph by choosing the best transition word for each blank.
vocabulary: por lo tanto: muestra un resultado
frames: The word ___ adds a new idea.
activities.prompt: Fill in the transitions that connect the ideas.

segments.text: , it can save families money. Some people think recycling takes too long.

activities.correct: Correct. "In addition" adds an idea, "However" shows a difference, and "Therefore" shows a result.
activities.hint: Decide if the sentence ADDS an idea, shows a DIFFERENCE, or gives a RESULT.
activities.support: Match the transition to the job: add, contrast, or conclude.
activities.extension: Write one new sentence using the transition "for example."

teacher.function: Selecting transitions by relationship between ideas.
teacher.lower: Tell students the job of each blank first.
teacher.challenge: Students rewrite a sentence with a different transition.
teacher.noTech: Print and fill the blanks by hand.
teacher.prompt: How did you know the second blank showed a difference?

activities.title: Pick All That Apply
activities.directions: Some test questions ask you to choose MORE THAN ONE answer. Choose every good test-taking habit.
vocabulary: hábito: algo que haces con frecuencia
frames: I chose ___ because it helps me ___.
activities.prompt: Which of these are GOOD test-taking habits? Choose all that apply.

options.text: Read every question before you answer.
Cross out answers you know are wrong.
Check your work if you have time.

activities.correct: Correct. Reading carefully, crossing out wrong answers, and checking your work are strong habits.
activities.hint: One choice is a BAD habit. "Select all" means more than one can be right.
activities.support: On select-all items, judge each choice on its own as good or bad.
activities.extension: Add one more good habit you use during a test.

teacher.function: Selecting all correct options.
teacher.lower: Read each habit and ask good or bad.
teacher.challenge: Students rank the habits from most to least helpful.
teacher.noTech: Read aloud; students check the good habits.
teacher.prompt: Why is guessing quickly a weak habit?

activities.title: Plan a Spoken Answer
activities.directions: Read the topic. Write planning notes, then practice saying your answer in complete sentences.
activities.prompt: Topic: Should students have a longer lunch break? Plan an answer with an opinion and two reasons.
activities.correct: Response saved. A strong spoken answer states an opinion and gives two clear reasons.
activities.hint: Start with your opinion, then give two reasons with "because."
activities.support: Use the frames: opinion, reason one, reason two, conclusion.
activities.extension: Add a sentence that answers someone who disagrees.

teacher.function: Planning and delivering an organized opinion.
teacher.lower: Give students an opinion outline to fill.
teacher.challenge: Students add a counterpoint and respond.
teacher.noTech: Students speak to a partner using the frames.
teacher.prompt: Which reason was strongest, and why?

successCriteria: Address the task: Topic: Should students have a longer lunch break? Plan an answer with an opinion and two reasons.
State a clear choice or position.
Connect a relevant reason or example to that position.

activities.title: Test-Taking Strategies
activities.directions: Read each strategy. Check the box, then write one example of how you will use it on the ACCESS test.

sheet.heading: Before You Start
items: Read the directions slowly before you begin. Underline the key word.
Look at how many questions there are and plan your time.
Take a slow breath and remind yourself: I have practiced for this.

sheet.heading: While You Work
items: Read the whole question before choosing an answer.
Cross out answers you know are wrong, then choose from what is left.
If a question is hard, mark it, skip it, and come back later.
For listening, write a key word as soon as you hear it.

sheet.heading: Before You Finish
items: Check that you answered every question.
Review any items you marked to come back to.
Make sure your writing has complete sentences and end marks.

teacher.use: Strategy reference and reflection sheet before a practice test.
teacher.function: Reviewing and personalizing test strategies.
teacher.lower: Read each strategy aloud; students restate it.
teacher.onLevel: Students add one example per strategy.
teacher.challenge: Students rank the three most useful strategies.
teacher.noTech: Print and complete by hand.
teacher.prompt: Which strategy will help you most, and why?

activities.title: Academic Vocabulary for ACCESS
activities.directions: Study each word and its meaning. Then write one sentence that uses the word correctly.

sheet.heading: Direction Verbs
items: analyze — break something into parts and study each part
compare — tell how two things are alike
contrast — tell how two things are different
summarize — give the main points in a few words
explain — tell why or how something happens

sheet.heading: Reading Words
items: main idea — the most important point of a text
detail — a small piece of information that supports the main idea
evidence — proof from the text
infer — figure out something using clues

sheet.heading: Writing Words
items: topic sentence — the sentence that names the big idea
transition — a word that links ideas, such as however or in addition
conclusion — the closing sentence or idea

teacher.use: Academic-vocabulary study sheet for test prep.
teacher.function: Studying and applying academic words.
teacher.lower: Review five words at a time; students echo meanings.
teacher.onLevel: Students write one sentence per word.
teacher.challenge: Students group words by domain (reading/writing).
teacher.noTech: Print as a study guide for home.
teacher.prompt: Which word do you see most often on tests?

activities.title: Full-Test Answer Sheet & Bubble Practice
activities.directions: Practice filling in the bubble for each answer completely and neatly. Use the practice rows below.

sheet.heading: How to Bubble
items: Fill in the whole circle, not just a check mark.
Make your mark dark and stay inside the circle.
Erase fully if you change your answer.
Match the question number to the same number on the answer sheet.

sheet.heading: Practice Rows (fill the chosen letter)
items: 1.   A    B    C    D
2.   A    B    C    D
3.   A    B    C    D
4.   A    B    C    D
5.   A    B    C    D

sheet.heading: Check Yourself
items: Did you fill one bubble per row?
Are all your marks dark and neat?
Did your row number match the question number?

teacher.function: Practicing accurate answer-sheet marking.
teacher.lower: Model filling one bubble on the board.
teacher.challenge: Students self-check using the checklist.
teacher.noTech: Print rows for hand practice.
teacher.prompt: Why does a clear, dark bubble matter on a scanned test?

activities.title: What Are the Directions Telling You?
wida: Determine the action a task requires
activities.directions: Read each test direction. Choose the answer that tells what you must DO.
activities.prompt: A test says: "Select the BEST answer and mark only one bubble." What should you do?

options.text: Pick the one answer that fits best and fill in a single bubble.
Mark every answer that could be true.
Write a paragraph explaining your choice.
Skip the question and come back later.

vocabulary: to choose one thing from a group
seleccionar: elegir una cosa de un grupo
the most correct choice of all the choices
mejor: la opción más correcta de todas
the small oval you fill in on an answer sheet
burbuja: el óvalo pequeño que rellenas en la hoja de respuestas
frames: The direction word ___ tells me to ___.
Because it says "only one," I will ___.
activities.correct: Yes. "Select the best" means choose one answer, and "only one bubble" means mark a single oval.
activities.hint: Underline the action verb and the number words like "one" or "all."
activities.support: Action words in directions: select = choose; mark = fill in; only one = a single answer.
activities.extension: Rewrite the direction in your own words for a younger student.

teacher.use: Open the set with direction-word decoding.
teacher.function: Interpreting the verb and quantity in a test direction.
teacher.lower: Read the direction aloud and point to the action verb.
teacher.challenge: Have students compare "select one" vs. "select all" directions.
teacher.noTech: Project the direction; students point to the verb and the number word.
teacher.prompt: Which word in the direction told you how many answers to mark?

activities.title: Cross Out What Cannot Be True
wida: Apply process of elimination to reading items
activities.directions: Read the short passage. Then choose every answer that you can ELIMINATE because the passage does not support it.
passage: Room 12 started a garden in March. The students planted tomatoes and beans. By June, the tomatoes were red and ready to pick. The beans were still growing.
activities.prompt: The question asks: "What was ready to pick in June?" Which answers can you ELIMINATE?

options.text: Beans, because they were still growing.
Tomatoes, because they were red and ready.
Corn, because corn is never mentioned.
Flowers, because flowers are never mentioned.

vocabulary: to remove a choice you know is wrong
eliminar: quitar una opción que sabes que está mal
to back up an answer with text proof
respaldar: apoyar una respuesta con pruebas del texto
a wrong answer made to look right
distractor: una respuesta incorrecta que parece correcta
frames: I can eliminate ___ because the text ___.
activities.correct: Correct. Beans were still growing, and corn and flowers are never in the passage, so all three can be eliminated.
activities.hint: Eliminate any choice the passage does not actually say.
activities.support: To eliminate: cross out answers that are off-topic or that the text says the opposite of.
activities.extension: Explain in one sentence why elimination makes the right answer easier to find.
readFor: words like still or not yet
names that never appear in the text

teacher.use: Teach elimination as a reading-test tool.
teacher.function: Removing unsupported distractors before choosing.

evidencia: hechos o palabras del texto que prueban una respuesta

to point to the exact words that prove your answer

the sentence that gives the reason

activities.title: Part B Listening 1
activities.testFormat: Listen to the school situation. Choose the best answer.
activities.directions: Choose why the teacher gives this direction.

activities.prompt: Why does the teacher say this?

activities.title: Part B Reading 1

activities.title: Part B Data Item

activities.directions: Read or listen carefully. Choose the best answer.

activities.title: Part B Science Language
activities.testFormat: Read a short science text and identify cause and effect.

activities.title: Read Between the Lines
activities.skill: Make an inference from the text
activities.directions: Read the passage. The answer is not stated directly. Use clues to choose the best inference.
vocabulary: pista: una señal en el texto
activities.prompt: Passage: Maria packed her umbrella and rain boots before school. She looked out the window and frowned. How does Maria most likely feel about the weather?
passage: Maria packed her umbrella and rain boots before school.
She looked out the window and frowned.

options.text: She is unhappy about the rain.
She is excited for a sunny day.
She forgot it was a school day.

activities.correct: Correct. The umbrella, boots, and frown are clues that Maria is unhappy about the rain.
activities.hint: The text does not say the feeling. Use the clue word "frowned."
activities.support: An inference uses clues. A frown is a clue about how someone feels.
activities.extension: Find another clue that shows it will rain.

teacher.function: Inferring a feeling from text clues.
teacher.lower: Underline the clue words together.
teacher.challenge: Students name two clues that support the answer.
teacher.noTech: Read aloud; students point to the clue.
teacher.prompt: What clue told you how Maria felt?

activities.title: Word Meaning in Context
activities.skill: Use context clues for word meaning
activities.directions: Read the passage. Use the words around each blank to choose the best meaning.
vocabulary: contexto: las palabras alrededor de una palabra
activities.prompt: Choose the meaning that fits the sentence.
passage: We wrapped the glass dishes in soft cloth because they were fragile.
Then we lifted an enormous couch that barely fit through the door.

segments.text: The dishes were fragile, which means they were
. The couch was enormous, which means it was

activities.correct: Correct. "Fragile" means easy to break, and "enormous" means very large.
activities.hint: Look at the words around each one: soft cloth and barely fit through the door.
activities.support: Context clues are the nearby words that hint at the meaning.
activities.extension: Use the word "fragile" in a new sentence.

teacher.function: Using context clues to define words.
teacher.lower: Read the clue words aloud first.
teacher.challenge: Students cover the word and predict the meaning.
teacher.noTech: Print and fill the blanks by hand.
teacher.prompt: Which nearby words gave you the meaning?

Read the directions on the screen.
Answer each question.
Click submit when you finish.

activities.title: What Is the Question Asking?

vocabulary: explicar: decir por qué o cómo
activities.prompt: A question says: "Explain why the character changed." What should you do?

options.text: Give the reasons the character changed.
Draw a picture of the character.

activities.correct: Correct. "Explain" asks you to give reasons — why or how.
activities.hint: The verb is "explain." It asks for reasons, not just a list.
activities.support: Match the verb to the task: explain = give reasons; identify = name; describe = tell about.
activities.extension: What would the question ask if the verb were "describe"?

teacher.lower: Underline the verb in the question.
teacher.challenge: Students rewrite the task for a different verb.
teacher.noTech: Read aloud; students point to the matching action.
teacher.prompt: How is "explain" different from "identify"?

activities.title: Topic Sentence or Detail?
activities.directions: Decide whether each sentence is a TOPIC sentence (the big idea) or a DETAIL (a small fact).
vocabulary: específico: sobre una sola cosa pequeña
a group of sentences about one idea
párrafo: un grupo de oraciones sobre una idea

items.text: Dogs make wonderful pets for many reasons.
My dog wags his tail when I come home.
Exercise keeps the body healthy in several ways.
Running for ten minutes raised my heart rate.

activities.correct: Strong work. Topic sentences are broad; details are small specific facts.
activities.hint: A topic sentence could open a whole paragraph. A detail is one small fact.
activities.support: If a sentence is broad enough to start a paragraph, it is a topic sentence.
activities.extension: Write a detail that supports the topic sentence about dogs.

teacher.lower: Sort only the dog sentences first.
teacher.challenge: Students write one detail for each topic sentence.

activities.title: Smart Test Choices

vocabulary: administrar el tiempo: usar bien tu tiempo
activities.prompt: You reach a hard question and only 10 minutes are left. What is the smartest choice?

options.text: Mark it, skip ahead, and come back if there is time.
Stop the whole test and give up.
Spend all 10 minutes on that one question.

activities.correct: Correct. Skip the hard one, answer the rest, and come back if time allows.
activities.hint: Think about what gets you the MOST questions answered.
activities.support: Good time management means not getting stuck on one hard item.
activities.extension: How could you mark a question so you remember to return?

teacher.lower: Talk through what each choice costs.
teacher.challenge: Students explain a time plan for a 30-minute test.
teacher.noTech: Read aloud; students vote on the smartest choice.
teacher.prompt: Why is getting stuck on one question risky?

activities.title: What Happened First?

activities.title: How Should You Spend Your Time?

Guess randomly on the rest and stop reading.
Leave Question 4 blank forever and never come back.

vocabulary: to use something carefully so it is enough
administrar: usar algo con cuidado para que alcance
to pass over something for now and return later
saltar: pasar por alto algo por ahora y volver después
the speed you work at so you finish on time
ritmo: la velocidad a la que trabajas para terminar a tiempo
frames: If I am stuck, I will ___ and come back.
activities.correct: Yes. Mark the hard one, keep your pace, and return with your leftover time.

activities.prompt: Choose the correct word form so each test sentence makes sense.
vocabulary: to make an idea clear with words
explicar: aclarar una idea con palabras

observar: notar detalles mirando con atención

respaldar: apoyar una afirmación con pruebas

vocabulary: the question part that tells you what to do
enunciado: la parte de la pregunta que te dice qué hacer
based on what the text or speaker says
según: basado en lo que dice el texto o el hablante
the order in which things happen

teacher.noTech: Write stems on cards; students physically sort them into three piles.
teacher.prompt: Which signal words told you the question wanted your opinion?

activities.title: Worksheet — Question-Stem Decoder
activities.directions: Print this page. Read each stem and write what it asks you to do.

sheet.heading: Circle the Signal Word
items: 1. According to the passage, who solved the problem?  (according to / who / problem)
2. List the steps in order.  (list / order / steps)
3. Do you agree? Support your answer.  (agree / support / answer)

sheet.heading: Name the Task
items: 4. "What time does the bus leave?" asks me to: ___
5. "Why do you think the plan worked?" asks me to: ___
6. "Put the events in sequence" asks me to: ___

sheet.heading: Time & Bubbles
items: 7. You have 20 minutes for 10 questions. About how long per question? ___
8. Practice: fill in bubble C for Question 1.  (A) (B) (C) (D)

sheet.heading: Write
items: Write one sentence telling how a signal word helps you answer faster: ___.
